design_reasoning.rationale: The plugin protocol compares in-process and isolated execution and defines compatibility and deprecation trade-offs.

observable_requirements.description: Compare plugin loading alternatives and trace compatibility, trust, and migration decisions.
Implement the selected versioned protocol and bounded lifecycle through the public host interface.

architecture_maintainability.rationale: Discovery, manifest validation, capability policy, lifecycle, and diagnostics use stable public interfaces.

observable_requirements.description: Coordinate plugins only through versioned manifests and bounded lifecycle hooks.
Validate protocol version, identifiers, capabilities, and lifecycle declarations.
Exercise compatible, deprecated, unknown, and malformed protocol versions.

security_by_design.rationale: The kit treats plugins as untrusted and gates declared capabilities while clearly documenting in-process limits.

observable_requirements.description: Map malicious manifests, capability escalation, lifecycle failure, and supply-chain risk to controls.
Deny undeclared or host-forbidden capabilities before plugin initialization.

testing_evidence.rationale: Tests cover protocol compatibility, capability denial, lifecycle rollback, malformed plugins, and deterministic diagnostics.

observable_requirements.description: Exercise supported, deprecated, future, and malformed manifest versions.
Exercise undeclared, forbidden, duplicated, and empty capability requests.
Exercise initialization failure, reverse-order cleanup, and bounded diagnostic output.

documentation_operations.rationale: Consumer installation, authoring, compatibility, diagnostics, migration, failure, and recovery guidance are complete.

observable_requirements.description: Document installation, host configuration, discovery, and diagnostic interpretation.
Document manifest fields, lifecycle hooks, capability requests, and test fixtures.
Document failed initialization, quarantine, rollback, cleanup, and recovery.
Document protocol deprecation, compatibility windows, and consumer migration steps.

repository_hygiene.rationale: The reusable package includes a recognized license, locks, CI, release provenance, contribution, and security policies.

observable_requirements.description: Commit deterministic dependency resolution for reproducible package review.
Publish a recognized open-source license permitting use, modification, and redistribution.
Define unit, compatibility, and package checks without claiming execution success.
Define tagged release provenance and immutable package publication inputs.
Document compatibility, tests, changesets, and review expectations.
Document supported versions and private vulnerability disclosure.

implemented_safeguards.threat: A plugin requests undeclared or host-forbidden access during initialization.
implemented_safeguards.control: The host intersects manifest declarations with an explicit host allowlist before invoking lifecycle hooks.

implemented_safeguards.threat: A partially initialized plugin leaves earlier resources active after a later hook fails.
implemented_safeguards.control: The host records completed hooks and invokes bounded reverse-order cleanup after initialization failure.

negative_boundary_cases.behavior: Reject a plugin manifest using an unsupported future protocol version.
Reject plugin initialization when a requested capability is forbidden by the host.
Clean up completed lifecycle hooks after a later initialization hook fails.

track_evidence.rationale: The project is a reusable, documented, licensed developer toolkit with a stable plugin surface and credible adoption path.

known_limitations.description: The reference host validates capabilities but does not provide operating-system process isolation.
Package registry signature and publisher identity verification remain consumer responsibilities.

excluded_runtime_claims: Whether the project builds or starts
Performance, scaling, or reliability under load
Ability to extend the system safely
